info.title: Agency Bulletin API
info.description:
# Introduction 
 
Welcome to the Agency Bulletin API (ABA) documentation. 


The ABA is designed to provide developers with a seamless and convenient way to access the latest weather bulletins 
published by the national meteorological agencies across the globe (e.g. NWS, UKMO, BoM) all in a standardized and 
easily interpretable GeoJSON format. By unifying the global weather bulletins data into one standardized API, 
we aim to simplify the process of working with such weather alerts, eliminating the need to understand 
multiple systems or formats. 


**Key Features**

* Unified access to latest weather bulletins from national meteorological agencies worldwide.
* Standardized GeoJSON format for all the weather bulletins, eliminating the need to grapple with various 
data formats and data pipelines, facilitating easy data visualization and integration with mapping and GIS solutions. 
* Exact geometries of affected areas' polygons included in the response, facilitating precise and granular 
mapping of weather bulletins.
* Inclusion of a Common Alerting Protocol (CAP) section in our GeoJSON response, preserving the original CAP data 
when issued by a national agency.

**Applications**

This API caters to a wide range of users and applications, including:

* Emergency alert systems
* Software developers building weather applications
* Travel planning websites
* Climate research projects 


This interactive documentation will get you up to speed on setting up requests, understanding responses, 
and leveraging the DTN Weather API for your needs.


# Getting Started
## Obtaining Credentials 
To start making requests, you will first need your API credentials that includes your client ID and client secret. 
Please contact an account manager or the [DTN sales team](https://www.dtn.com/contact-us/) to obtain these. 
Then, review the `Authentication` section to learn how to request an API access token. Do not share or use others' 
API credentials, since doing so may compromise information security.

## Making requests
Starting off your journey with the the Agency Bulletin API (ABA) couldn't be easier. 
We've provided a variety of options to suit your needs and comfort level:
Interactive Documentation: Our interactive documentation is a great starting point. 
Simply navigate to the "Authentication" section, insert your credentials, and you'll obtain an access token behind 
the scenes. Then, explore the API endpoints described in the Endpoints section.

**a) Interactive Documentation:** Our interactive documentation is a great starting point. Simply navigate to 
the `Authentication` section, insert your credentials, and you'll obtain an access token behind the scenes. 
Then, explore the API endpoints described in the `Endpoints` section.

**b) Postman Collection:** If you prefer a more hands-on approach, consider downloading [this Postman collection](https://dtn.box.com/s/vpuanadvzarpfvh8jujq1hue0ikjxfom) 
After inserting your credentials, you can start testing and using the API in a highly interactive 
environment.

**c) Writing Code:** Ready to start coding? Try the Python example below, 
replacing `client_id` and `client_secret` with proper credentials. 
This invokes the /bulletins endpoint with a GET request and prints the response.





```python
#--- Obtain an API access token ---
import requests

# --- Obtain an API access token ---
auth_url = 'https://api.auth.dtn.com/v1/tokens/authorize'
body = {
    'grant_type': 'client_credentials',
    'client_id': '...insert your client id here...',
    'client_secret': '...insert your client secret here...',
    'audience': 'https://weather.api.dtn.com'
}

response = requests.post(auth_url, json=body)
access_token = response.json()['data']['access_token']

# --- Invoke the API ---
api_base_url = 'https://wxbulletin.api.dtn.com/v2'
query_parameters = '&'.join([
    'showTotal=True',
    'country=US',
    'excludeGeometry=True',
    'agency=NWS',
])

endpoint = '/bulletins?' + query_parameters
headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + access_token}
response = requests.get(api_base_url + endpoint, headers=headers)

# --- Print the response ---
print(response.json())          
```

get.description:
```shell 
GET https://wxbulletin.api.dtn.com/v2/bulletins
```

This endpoint returns the latest active weather bulletins from the requested national meteorological agency. 
It is the primary source of information for real-time weather alerts and updates.

Understanding and Utilizing Key Query Parameters:
- **Country:** 
Use this parameter to access all active weather bulletins within a specific country. 
This parameter accepts ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes.
Example: country=US

- **startTime:**
This parameter allows you to filter alerts sent from a specific date and time onward, 
returning all subsequent alerts. It requires timestamps in ISO 8601 date-time format as specified in RFC 3339.
Example: startTime=2022-11-25T00:00:00

- **endTime:**
Use this parameter to receive alerts up to a specific timestamp, 
filtering out any alerts sent after this date and time. The expected format is ISO 8601 date-time as per RFC 3339.
Example: endTime=2022-11-26T00:00:00

- **excludeGeometry:**
This parameter is crucial and is set to false by default, meaning the response will include detailed geometry of the 
polygons corresponding to each active warning. This can be particularly useful for understanding the exact impacted 
areas or for visualizing warnings in GIS applications. However, be mindful that including this detailed information 
might substantially increase the payload size when dealing with numerous active bulletins. 
If you prefer to exclude the detailed geometry and reduce payload size, set this parameter to true.

Query Example: `https://wxbulletin.api.dtn.com/v2/bulletins?country=US&showTotal=true&agency=NWS&startTime=2023-09-25T12:45:00&endTime=2023-09-25T12:47:00`

```shell 
GET https://wxbulletin.api.dtn.com/v2/metadata
```
This endpoint provides metadata from each national meteorological agency, 
detailing what events are published and in which languages, allowing developers to understand the range and scope of 
available bulletins.

Understanding and Utilizing Key Query Parameters:

- Access this endpoint to retrieve a comprehensive list of all available meteorological agencies, 
the events they publish, and the languages they support. As we continuously integrate support for new agencies into 
this API, this endpoint serves as an excellent resource to stay updated on the most recent agencies and 
their corresponding published events.
- event: Use this parameter to pinpoint a particular event. It also aids in identifying which agencies 
broadcast that specific event type.

Query Example: `https://wxbulletin.api.dtn.com/v2/metadata?country=US&event=Flash`

clientCredentials.description:
# Using DAIS for M2M/API Auth
You have been given a Client ID and a Client Secret, which are used to request a DTN Access Token. DTN Access Tokens are required when making calls to each and every DTN API endpoint. The following information provides additional details on these tokens and how they are generated.
## What is an Access Token and how is it different from an API Key?
An API Key is a random string of characters that an API uses to authorize whether or not a calling client has approved access to an endpoint. These keys are a non-standard approach to API authorization and are generally issued on a per-API basis.

An Access Token is also a string of characters but is a base-64 encoded JavaScript Object Notation Web Token, or JWT. JWTs are a widely accepted standard that use OAuth concepts and approaches. 

Both API Keys and Access Tokens are used in an Authorization Request Header as a Bearer, meaning there is no difference in where you put this string of characters when you make calls to DTN APIs.
## How to generate an Access Token?
When requested, an Access Token is generated for your specific Client (ID/Secret) and for a specific API. The DTN Auth and Identity Service (DAIS) generates new Access Tokens for your client. The DAIS endpoint is `POST https://api.auth.dtn.com/v1/tokens/authorize`.

This endpoint takes two Header parameters:
  * `Content-Type: application/json`
  * `Accept: application/json`

This endpoint takes four parameters in the Request Body:
  * `grant_type`: this should always be client_credentials for generating machine-to-machine tokens.
  * `client_id`: this is the Client ID or Application ID using the token and is given to you by DTN's Identity Team. This ID will never change for your client/application.
  * `client_secret`: this is the Client Secret that is associated with the Application ID and is given to you by DTN's Identity Team. This key is subject to rotation for security purposes but always with the client's knowledge.
  * `audience`: this is the API for which this Access Token will be used. For the DTN Agency Bulletin API, you need to use the following audience: https://weather.api.dtn.com

You can use this CURL command template as a reference for obtaining an access token:
  ```
  curl --location --request POST 'https://api.auth.dtn.com/v1/tokens/authorize' \
--header 'Accept: application/json' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '{
"grant_type": "client_credentials",
"client_id": "insert your client id here",
"client_secret": "insert your client secret here",
"audience": "insert your audience here"
}' 
  ```

*This document, for demonstration purposes, supplies a client_id and client_secret in all code examples. This client/application is for a fictitious API and cannot be used in practice to gain unauthorized access to any other DTN API.*
Upon generating a new Access Token, you should receive an HTTP Response from DAIS similar to this:
  ```
  {
    "data": {
          "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCIsImtpZCI6InpfX21pZW13NGhoTmdvQWQxR3N6ciJ9..0VHdyp1w9PPFVI0FPheAwuKZwb5C25rwP-LPMXcSNoRmouvga1DZtNLA67ZzE_sAlc_VpaDRr6daLKr_Alw4347mw9sdjP8wKR27kCZa9JZK5PGQMmXHscATbzBEJYpCPklfyGaajgymqTBGnedcv8F0UvlRzQPsFeRPnVoX7BWOSXpMbyToGiXWkQLBQT7r96KAmLZOPJFZspPtjw-wH2mSL2WNa_nkB4j5vMGhGxlKiNRsKb30TH_WAel2hsxNlcPK3XHCmrMTYsNnu7HNqOTMn2i0__0rvBrhSWEw-_grqQDmWFJuWd7Qhi1q81AaJcdqgoSa_efz93QFclJUNw",
          "scope": "read:demo create:demo update:demo",
          "expires_in": 90,
          "token_type": "Bearer"
      },
      "meta": {
          "date_time": "2022-06-24T19:09:42.963Z",
          "name": "v1.tokens.authorize",
          "uuid": "ee6f9feb-dcf8-4421-a6fd-efd6beabdaa9",
          "start_timestamp": 1656097782509,
          "end_timestamp": 1656097782963,
          "execution_time": 454
      }
  }
  ```
Looking at this Response, you will see:
  * `access_token`: contains the JWT Access Token string you will use as your Bearer token.
  * `scope`: contains the scopes that this Access Token gives you permissions to access.
  * `expires_in`: contains the length of time before this Access Token will expire, in seconds.
  * `token_type`: verifies that this Access Token should be used as a Bearer token.

## How to use an Access Token after one is generated?
Once a new Access Token is obtained, it is used in each call to a DTN API endpoint as a Bearer token in an Authorization Request Header. For example:
  ```
  Header: 'Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCIsImtpZCI6InpfX21pZW13NGhoTmdvQWQxR3N6ciJ9..0VHdyp1w9PPFVI0FPheAwuKZwb5C25rwP-LPMXcSNoRmouvga1DZtNLA67ZzE_sAlc_VpaDRr6daLKr_Alw4347mw9sdjP8wKR27kCZa9JZK5PGQMmXHscATbzBEJYpCPklfyGaajgymqTBGnedcv8F0UvlRzQPsFeRPnVoX7BWOSXpMbyToGiXWkQLBQT7r96KAmLZOPJFZspPtjw-wH2mSL2WNa_nkB4j5vMGhGxlKiNRsKb30TH_WAel2hsxNlcPK3XHCmrMTYsNnu7HNqOTMn2i0__0rvBrhSWEw-_grqQDmWFJuWd7Qhi1q81AaJcdqgoSa_efz93QFclJUNw'
  ```

## Deconstructing the Access Token
A DTN Access Token carries information within its JWT Body that is available on every API call. By deconstructing the JWT token, our Access Tokens will resemble:
  ```
  {
    "https://auth.dtn.com/customerId": "1234567890Demo",
    "https://auth.dtn.com/productCode": "DemoApiP",
    "https://auth.dtn.com/requesterIp": "18.213.174.27",
    "https://auth.dtn.com/rps": "100",
    "https://auth.dtn.com/tier": "Basic",
    "https://auth.dtn.com/quota": "999999",
    "iss": "https://id.auth.dtn.com/",
    "sub": "nfyO3KiKPR8N0DKR5CL8jS9GFBCDeyFM@clients",
    "aud": "https://demo-api.auth.dtn.com/",
    "iat": 1656099068,
    "exp": 1656099158,
    "azp": "nfyO3KiKPR8N0DKR5CL8jS9GFBCDeyFM",
    "scope": "read:demo create:demo update:demo",
    "gty": "client-credentials",
    "permissions": [
      "read:demo",
      "create:demo",
      "update:demo"
    ]
  }
  ```
### Description of Claims

  | Claim                              | Type                                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
  | -----------------------------------| --------------------------------------------| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
  | `https://auth.dtn.com/customerId`  | String                                      | Custom DTN claim containing the Customer ID found in the DTN Order Management/Salesforce system associated with this token.                                                                                                |
  | `https://auth.dtn.com/productCode` | String                                      | Custom DTN claim containing the Identity product code associated with this token.                                                                                                                                          |
  | `https://auth.dtn.com/requesterIp` | String                                      | Custom DTN claim containing the IP address of the requesting client.                                                                                                                                                       |
  | `https://auth.dtn.com/rps`         | String                                      | Custom DTN claim containing the maximum rate per second this customer is authorized to utilize.                                                                                                                            |
  | `https://auth.dtn.com/tier`        | String                                      | Custom DTN claim containing the data tier the customer purchased for the requested access.                                                                                                                                 |
  | `https://auth.dtn.com/quota`       | String                                      | Custom DTN claim containing the maximum yearly quota the customer purchased for calling DTN endpoints for the specific product.                                                                                            |
  | `iss`                              | String (URI)                                | The Security Token Service (STS) that issues and returns the token. If this value is not from `https://id.auth.dtn.com/`, the token should not be considered trusted.                                                      |
  | `sub`                              | String (URI)                                | The principle about which the token asserts information (the User ID or Client ID within the Identity Provider). A User ID will start with a prefix of `auth0\|`, while the Client ID will end with the suffix `@clients`. |
  | `aud`                              | String \| Array (Strings) (URI \| [URI, …]) | Identifies the intended recipient(s) of the token – its audience. The token should be rejected if the audience does not contain values expected by the calling application.                                                |
  | `iat`                              | Number (Timestamp)                          | “Issued At” indicates when the authentication for this token occurred.                                                                                                                                                     |
  | `exp`                              | Number (Timestamp)                          | The “expiration time” on or after which the JWT must not be accepted for processing.                                                                                                                                       |
  | `azp`                              | String                                      | The application/client ID of the client using the token. The application can cat as itself or on behalf of a user.                                                                                                         |
  | `gty`                              | String (Space-delimited)                    | The grant type that was used to request the token – not an RFC 7519 registered claim (Auth0-specific).                                                                                                                     |
  | `permissions`                      | Array (Strings)                             | The grant type that was used to request the token – not an RFC 7519 registered claim (Auth0-specific).                                                                                                                     |

tags.description: The the Agency Bulletin API (ABA) is designed around two major endpoints, each offering unique functionalities tailored to your diverse weather bulletin data needs. Whether you require forecast and historical data for a single location, data for multiple location/timestamp pairs, or the associated metadata, our API has got you covered.
